verdict.rationale: Harbor Compliance publishes a large, public OpenAPI v3 document (about 681K chars, including registered-agent-deliveries endpoints). It supports OAuth client-credentials auth, idempotency keys and documented rate limits, which shows a substantial programmatic surface. However, create, update and delete operations need capabilities that Harbor Compliance must explicitly grant per account, so UI-equivalent write access is not available by default. Nothing shows that the many UI features (Entity/License/Tax/Records Managers, interactive map, Compliance Navigator AI, filing search) are exposed through the API. Missing for 10: an explicit API/UI parity claim, default self-serve write access, documented API coverage of each UI module (map, Navigator AI, requirement search, records, profile updates), and independent or hands-on corroboration.
